drafted_from: tool:hear-for-a-device row in tools/listen-for-a-while/tool-rows.json, hearForADevice and hearPieces in read-data/listen-for-a-while.mjs, and the test in test/listen-for-a-while.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Hear the recording /Recordings/phone-piece.m4a that my Phone made at 2026-10-31T12:00:00Z, call the listening p1, and use the Whisper model I keep at ~/models/ggml-base.bin." It runs tool:hear-for-a-device and tells you how many turns it kept.
no_lists_because: It writes heard rows and voice-session rows through the records door, but it names no list of yours; the rows are its own record kinds.
instructions: 1. Put the recording in your files (the door finds it by name) and have a ggml Whisper model file and the whisper-cli and ffmpeg programs on the computer that will hear it; enrol the voices you want named with tool:enrol-a-voice-or-face first.

2. Say "Hear the recording <file> that my <device> made at <time>" with the model path; your AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:hear-for-a-device (file, device and model_path are required; at, listening and write_back are optional).

3. Read the answer: pieces, turns and rows_written count what was heard and kept as one heard row per turn; let_go and blocked say when a recording rule or a pause let the piece go unheard; leaves and stays list what leaves this computer and what stays.
4. Use the same listening name to continue an earlier listening so unknown voices keep their numbers (voice-1 stays voice-1); add write_back true to get <file>.speakers.json beside the recording.

worked_examples.title: A phone's recording becomes one heard row
worked_examples.ask: Hear the recording my Phone made at noon on 31 October and keep who said what.
worked_examples.given: From tools/listen-for-a-while/test/listen-for-a-while.test.mjs (the test replaces hearing and naming with stand-ins): the door holds /Recordings/phone-piece.m4a, the hearing step returns one stretch from 1 s to 2 s with the text "from the phone", and the naming step labels it Someone (voice-1).
worked_examples.hands_back: One heard row with id heard:p1:1793448001000 (the start time plus 1 s) whose device is Phone and text is "from the phone"; the answer says listening "p1", pieces 1, turns 1, rows_written 1, left_out 0, let_go 0, blocked null, paused null, heard_until "2026-10-31T12:00:00.000Z", with the leaves and stays lists. The copy read for hearing is deleted; the recording in your files is left where it is and nothing is deleted from it. Without device the run refuses with "Say which device recorded this"; without file with "Give `file`".
